Abstract.AbstractText: The aim of study was to design, statistically optimize and characterize Granisetron HCl loaded transfersomal gel for transdermal delivery, in order to overcome the side effects associated with oral delivery. A response surface methodology experimental design was applied for the optimization of transfersomes, using Box-Behnken experimental design. Phospholipid-90G, sodium deoxycholate and sonication time, each at three levels, were selected as independent variables, and while entrapment efficiency, vesicle size and transdermal flux were identified as dependent variables. The formulation was characterized for surface morphology and shape, particle size and zeta potential. Ex-vivo transdermal flux was determined using Franz-diffusion cell assembly, with rat skin a barrier medium. The optimized transfersomes formulation (GTV-16) incorporated into gel which was found spherical, unilamellar structures, with a homogeneous distribution and low polydispersity index (0.292). During evaluation nano-transformal gel has good particle size of 127.7±1.08 nm, better entrapment efficiency of 83.0±3.22 % and transdermal flux of 20.0±1.88 µg/cm2/hour. The results demonstrated Granisetron Hydrochloride loaded nano-gel significantly superior in terms of amount of drug permeated through the skin, with enhancement ratio of 8.5 when compared with drug solution, further considered for drug delivery development.
